title: MVCC, transactions, snapshots and VACUUM
one_liner: Postgres keeps many versions of each row, uses snapshots to decide which version you see, and VACUUM cleans up old versions.
analogy: Like a shared Google Doc with version history: readers view a frozen version, writers add new versions, and a janitor deletes versions nobody needs.
big_picture: Every row version (tuple) stores xmin (who created it) and xmax (who deleted or locked it).
UPDATE never edits in place. It writes a new tuple and marks the old one with xmax.
A snapshot is a list of which transactions counted as finished when you started looking.
Visibility check: xmin must be committed and finished before my snapshot, and xmax must not be. Then I see the tuple.
Commit status lives in pg_xact (clog), 2 bits per xid. Hint bits cache it on the tuple.
VACUUM removes dead tuples nobody can see, and freezes old xids to prevent wraparound.

flow.detail: An xid is handed out only when you first write. Reads need no xid.
BEGIN, COMMIT and ABORT map onto a layered state machine.
Scans the list of running backends and records xmin, xmax and the in-progress xip list.

flow.step: Snapshot is managed per isolation level
flow.detail: Read Committed takes a new one per statement. Repeatable Read and up keep one for the whole transaction.
The scan asks if this tuple version is visible to my snapshot.
Commit writes a WAL record, then flips the xid status to committed in pg_xact.
On reads, heap_page_prune_opt calls heap_page_prune_and_freeze. HOT chains collapse. Only VACUUM turns LP_DEAD into LP_UNUSED, after index cleanup.

flow.step: VACUUM scans, vacuums indexes, then heap
flow.detail: Collect dead TIDs, clean indexes, mark heap line pointers unused, freeze old tuples.
A launcher starts workers that vacuum tables crossing thresholds or nearing wraparound.

diagram.claim: A write creates a tuple version, a snapshot decides visibility, and VACUUM reclaims dead versions.

interview.q: What are xmin and xmax on a tuple?
answer: xmin is the xid that inserted this tuple version.
xmax is the xid that deleted or locked it, or 0 if none.
Flags like HEAP_XMIN_COMMITTED in htup_details.h cache their status.
interview.trap: xmax is not only for deletes. It is also used for row locks like SELECT FOR UPDATE.

interview.q: What does an UPDATE do physically?
answer: It inserts a new tuple version with new xmin.
It sets xmax on the old tuple to the updating xid.
Code is heap_update in heapam.c.
The old version stays until VACUUM or pruning removes it.
interview.trap: UPDATE does not overwrite the row in place.

answer: It is a struct (SnapshotData in snapshot.h) with xmin, xmax and a list xip of in-progress xids.
xid below xmin: finished. xid at or above xmax: invisible, started later.
xids in xip were running at snapshot time, so invisible.

interview.q: Where is commit status stored and how is it read?
answer: pg_xact (clog.c) stores 2 bits per xid: in progress, committed, aborted, sub-committed.
TransactionIdDidCommit in transam.c reads it.
Visibility code sets hint bits on the tuple so the next reader skips the clog lookup.
interview.trap: Hint bits need no WAL for correctness, since pg_xact can recreate them. With checksums or wal_log_hints on, the first hint change after a checkpoint may log a full page.

answer: Did xmin commit before my snapshot was taken (not in xip, below xmax)? If not, invisible.
Is xmax invalid, aborted, or not yet visible to me? Then the tuple is visible.
If xmax committed and visible to my snapshot, the tuple is deleted for me.
Own-transaction changes use the command id so you see earlier commands only.

interview.q: How do isolation levels differ in snapshots?
answer: Read Committed takes a fresh snapshot for each statement.
Repeatable Read keeps one snapshot for the whole transaction.
IsolationUsesXactSnapshot() in xact.h checks for level at or above Repeatable Read.
Serializable adds predicate locking on top.
interview.trap: Postgres Read Uncommitted behaves like Read Committed. There are no dirty reads.

answer: Heap-Only Tuple: update where no indexed column changes and the page has room.
The new tuple is flagged HEAP_ONLY_TUPLE and old HEAP_HOT_UPDATED.
No new index entries. Index points at the chain root.
Pruning can reclaim dead chain members without VACUUM.
See README.HOT and pruneheap.c.

interview.q: What does VACUUM do and why can it not remove everything?
answer: It finds dead tuples, removes their index entries, then frees heap slots (lazy_vacuum_heap_rel).
Dead means no snapshot can still see it. VACUUM computes cutoffs in vacuum_get_cutoffs. Pruning uses GlobalVisState from procarray.c.
ComputeXidHorizons in procarray.c finds the oldest running xmin.
A long-running transaction holds the horizon back and causes bloat.
interview.trap: VACUUM does not shrink the file normally. It marks space reusable. VACUUM FULL rewrites the table.

interview.q: What is xid wraparound and how is it prevented?
answer: xids are 32-bit and compared in a circle, so only about 2 billion are in the past.
Very old tuples would suddenly look like they are in the future.
VACUUM freezes old tuples (heap_prepare_freeze_tuple) so they are visible to all.
SetTransactionIdLimit in varsup.c sets warning and stop limits.
Autovacuum is forced when age passes autovacuum_freeze_max_age.
interview.trap: Turning autovacuum off does not stop anti-wraparound vacuum. It still runs.

contributor_tips: Read src/backend/access/transam/README and README.HOT first. They explain the design in plain English.
Run the isolation tester in src/test/isolation/specs to see concurrent snapshots behave. Add a spec for any visibility fix.
Be careful with visibility code. Small changes can cause silent data corruption, so reason about every xid state.
Start with vacuum.c and autovacuum.c for docs, logging or GUC tweaks before touching heapam_visibility.c.

glossary.meaning: 32-bit transaction id given to a transaction that writes.
A record of which transactions count as finished at one moment.
A flag on a tuple caching commit or abort status.
Cheap in-page cleanup of dead tuples and HOT chains.
Marking old tuples visible to everyone so xid age stops mattering.
Horizon: tuples deleted before it are invisible to all and removable.
